lines.text: If you toss your grandpa's dead watch, you could be tossing seventeen rubies.
Some people think a watch that stopped is just scrap metal.
But inside, its fastest parts spin on tiny lab-grown rubies.
Steel grinding on steel wears out fast. Steel on ruby barely wears at all.
That matters, because this little wheel swings up to eight times every second.
That's nearly seven hundred thousand swings a day, with no battery.
So even a dead one can be repaired, and collectors still want it.
So he scanned it first. Estimated resale: sixty to one hundred fifty dollars.
I used Scan For Worth. Check the drawer before the trash.
